title: POC weekly sync - application integration / SDK tool-function structured output - QuantifyTech

SE to run targeted latency/cost benchmarks and provide example payloads; customer to share additional sample data and error logs.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-04-22 15:00 PDT; Duration 45m; Attendees: Samir, Maya (Redwood); Lena, Ravi, Aisha (QuantifyTech)

[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check in how's the week been?
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: hi Samir, thanks, good. we ran the integration tests we talked about last week. saw a few parse failures on the structured output for order-confirmation flow. overall not terrible but need to tune.
[00:20] Maya Chen: thanks Lena. quick recap: last week's change was switching from freeform JSON extraction to function-calling with a strict schema using the redwood-js SDK. we also turned on prefix KV caching for repeated customer contexts.
[00:34] Ravi Kumar: yeah we integrated the SDK, small note our engineers saw an npm import warning, but it's just a minor thing. main issues were price field sometimes comes back as string with currency words, and order_id sometimes null in ~6% of cases.
[00:47] Aisha Malik: to add, product wants the structured payload to be 98% parseable, otherwise the downstream workflow breaks and manual review spikes.
[01:00] Samir Patel: got it. Maya, can you remind the team of how we're doing validation with function-calls?
[01:06] Maya Chen: sure. when you call the SDK function API you declare the schema for the function response. our function-calling layer will enforce types and return an error metadata field when output doesn't match. in practice we've seen two failure modes: 1) hallucinated/malformed fields (like extra text around the price) and 2) truncation when max_tokens is too low.
[01:28] Lena Ortiz: interesting, truncation might explain null order_ids; some of our examples are heavy — long product descriptions.
[01:35] Samir Patel: what's current max_tokens in the POC?
[01:38] Ravi Kumar: 256 right now for generation.
[01:40] Maya Chen: try bumping to 512 for those heavy flows; also set a stricter stop sequence and lower temperature to 0.0-0.2 for deterministic fields like ids/prices.
[01:53] Lena Ortiz: ok makes sense. our concern is cost and latency though — if we double tokens that might affect p95.
[01:59] Samir Patel: that's the classic tradeoff. we ran a small benchmark last night on Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted variants — p95 on hosted with current config was ~820ms, p50 ~220ms, average tokens per request ~420 which maps to roughly $0.012 per request in the POC pricing tier.
[02:20] Ravi Kumar: 820ms p95 is doable but in our SLA we target <700ms p95. any levers?
[02:25] Maya Chen: yes — three levers: 1) quantization/compact model variant to reduce latency, 2) smarter batching for high concurrency, 3) prefix KV caching to avoid re-encoding repeated context. for your flow I think prefix caching + moving some static context into the function input will help more than bumping tokens.
[02:43] Aisha Malik: when you say quantization, are we losing quality?
[02:46] Maya Chen: small risk. we recommend A/B testing quantized variant on a subset of traffic. Redwood Optimize has model/quantization suggestions per workload; we can run a quality regression test against your golden prompts.
[02:58] Samir Patel: I can coordinate the A/B test if you want.
[03:01] Lena Ortiz: yes please. also, about that parse error rate — we saw 92% parseable after switching to function-calls. want to push to 98. what are concrete steps?
[03:12] Maya Chen: two immediate steps: 1) tighten the output schema to mark price as number and currency code as enum; 2) add a small post-parse validation step in your app to normalize common patterns (e.g., strip "$" or whitespace). we can provide a snippet.
[03:27] Ravi Kumar: would be useful to see the SDK snippet. the current code uses the redwood-js client but we didn't use the function-defined schema correctly — we left the response_type loose.
[03:37] Samir Patel: I'll share an updated snippet after the call. sample link: https://redwood.example.com/qt-poc/sdk-examples (note: internal link).
[03:47] Aisha Malik: also security questions from our compliance team — they asked for SOC2, SSO instructions, and KMS integration notes.
[03:54] Samir Patel: we have SOC 2 and can share the packet; SSO/SAML docs and KMS/HSM integration notes too. I'll attach links.
[04:02] Maya Chen: another quick note: some of the transcription logs we saw had the model returning currency words like "USD dollars" which trips your enum. we can set the function schema to accept either number or string but then run conversion server-side. better to make the model output canonical via prompt templates.
[04:19] Lena Ortiz: can you give an example prompt template?
[04:22] Maya Chen: sure — we recommend an explicit instruction: "Return JSON ONLY matching the schema: {\"order_id\": integer, \"price\": number, \"currency\": string(ISO-4217)}. Do not include explanations or extra keys." then provide few-shot examples. keep temperature 0.0.
[04:40] Ravi Kumar: ok we'll try that. in our last run we used few-shot but with a high temperature (0.7) because we were exploring creative paraphrases, that likely caused instability.
[04:49] Samir Patel: easy fix. lower temp for production, keep higher temp for NLU/intent experiments.
[04:55] Aisha Malik: one more thing — we're integrating tool-calls where the model queries an internal prices service. latency there adds up; any suggestions?
[05:03] Maya Chen: for tool calls you have two patterns: sync RPC-style calls or async background calls. For price lookups, do local RPC with a small TTL cache on the agent side. Also consider pushing static price catalog into the prefix so the model doesn't always call the tool.
[05:19] Ravi Kumar: good idea. we do have a price catalog that updates hourly — could put the latest snapshot into KV cache.
[05:25] Lena Ortiz: what's the recommended approach to instrument failures so we can correlate parse errors to model responses in logs?
[05:31] Maya Chen: add correlation IDs from your app into the request metadata; Redwood tracing shows per-request token breakdown and has hooks to export the response + function call payload for debugging. we'll share a tracing snippet.
[05:45] Samir Patel: ok let's pivot to concrete asks — Maya, can you run an end-to-end benchmark with these variants: current config, +512 tokens, quantized model, and prefix caching enabled? aim for 1k requests across typical payloads.
[05:59] Maya Chen: yes I can. I'll run them on the Hosted and Dedicated stacks so you see the delta.
[06:05] Ravi Kumar: how long will that take?
[06:07] Maya Chen: I'll start today, expect results in 5 business days — will post p50/p95 + cost per request.
[06:14] Samir Patel: perfect. Lena, Ravi any blockers on you providing sample payloads?
[06:20] Ravi Kumar: none, we'll extract 100 representative payloads and highlight the failed ones.
[06:25] Aisha Malik: on security, can you also provide the IP allowlist and VPC peering doc?
[06:29] Samir Patel: yes, will include allowlist and VPC peering notes for Private deployment.
[06:34] Lena Ortiz: one compliance Q — for PII do you have redaction hooks?
[06:38] Maya Chen: Redwood has pre- and post-processing hooks. we can show an example lambda that strips PII before sending.
[06:45] Ravi Kumar: great. also, a small bug we saw: the SDK's retry backoff was causing duplicate function calls in rare cases. any known workarounds?
[06:54] Maya Chen: we have idempotency keys you can set at the request level. set request_id header and server will dedupe within a short window. we'll add that into the snippet.
[07:05] Samir Patel: thanks. quick recap before we close — action items: I'll send SDK snippet, SOC2/security docs, and links (redwood.example.com/qt-poc). Maya will run benchmarks and share metrics. Ravi will supply payloads and logs. set follow-up for 2027-04-30 to review benchmarks. sound right?
[07:25] Lena Ortiz: yes. thanks everyone.
[07:28] Aisha Malik: thanks.
[07:30] Samir Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up in threads. meeting end.

Notes: occasional transcription errors observed ("K-V cash" for KV cache, "RedWood Dedicate" for Redwood Dedicated). Links referenced rather than full artifacts: https://redwood.example.com/qt-poc/sdk-examples, https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-packet
